findings.title: AssignmentSource default queued timestamp is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: The dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now(). Python evaluates this default when the class is defined, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit queued value receives the same import-time datetime instead of the current time. This makes the field misleading for debugging and incorrect for any future logic that relies on it. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now).

findings.title: AssignmentSource.to_dict emits a datetime into Celery task kwargs
findings.body: sync_group_assignee_outbound passes assignment_source.to_dict() as the assignment_source_dict kwarg for the sync_assignee_outbound task. to_dict uses dataclasses.asdict, which leaves queued as a datetime object. Task kwargs are serialized across process boundaries; if the Celery serializer is JSON or another non-pickle serializer, this can raise TypeError and prevent the sync task from being enqueued. Even if it serializes to a string, AssignmentSource.from_dict does not parse it back into a datetime. Serialize queued to an ISO string, omit it, or explicitly handle conversion in from_dict.

findings.title: from_dict silently discards invalid assignment source and fails open
findings.body: AssignmentSource.from_dict catches TypeError and ValueError and returns None. The outbound cycle-prevention logic treats None as no source, so a malformed or partially serialized payload can cause outbound sync to run and potentially recreate the sync loop this PR is trying to prevent. At minimum, log or metric this failure; consider stricter validation or safer fallback behavior.

findings.title: Cycle suppression blocks all outbound syncs for the source integration, not just the source issue
findings.body: should_sync returns False whenever sync_source.integration_id matches the installation's integration, regardless of which external issue triggered the inbound change. If a Sentry group is linked to multiple external issues belonging to the same integration, an inbound assignment change from one issue suppresses outbound assignment updates to all other linked issues in that integration. This can leave linked external issues inconsistent. If the intent is only to avoid echoing back to the originating issue, AssignmentSource should also carry the external issue key and the check should be per issue.

findings.title: New task keyword argument is not backward compatible with older workers
findings.body: The Celery task sync_assignee_outbound now accepts assignment_source_dict, and producers immediately include it in apply_async kwargs. During a rolling deploy, a worker running the previous task signature will receive an unexpected keyword argument and fail with TypeError, causing sync tasks to error or retry. If task producers and workers can be deployed independently, additive task signature changes need compatibility handling or deploy-order guarantees.

findings.title: Missing coverage for deassignment with a matching assignment source
findings.body: The added tests cover assignment with a matching AssignmentSource, but there is no test that GroupAssignee.objects.deassign(..., assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)) suppresses outbound sync to the same integration. Since the PR changes the deassign path as well, this path should also be covered.
